[PERSISTENT EXPERIENCE GUIDANCE]
## Consolidated Experience from Similar Tasks
The key consolidated lessons are: (1) Never assume a pick-up will succeed. Before picking an object, navigate to its location and verify that it exists, is visible, and is within reach. If a find action fails, treat the object as unavailable and switch to exploration or an alternative rather than proceeding. (2) Never assume a place action is valid. Before placing, verify that the robot is actually holding the target object; if not, perform a successful pick first. (3) Never assume MoveAhead will succeed. Verify that the forward path is clear; if blocked, rotate, strafe, or choose an alternate route. In general, each action should be preceded by a precondition check and followed by confirmation of the expected state change.

## Preliminary Thinking
1. Locate the black table to confirm the target destination and its reachable placement surface. 2. For each object in order (plate, screwdriver, cleanser): navigate toward the object's last known or likely location, verify through scene inspection or a find action that the object is present and reachable, then pick it up. 3. After each pick, verify that the robot is holding the object. 4. Navigate to the black table, avoiding obstacles; if a forward move is blocked, rotate or strafe and continue. 5. Place the held object on the black table, then verify that it is no longer held and has been placed. 6. Repeat steps 2–5 for the next object. If any object cannot be found, search nearby plausible locations or switch to exploration before abandoning it; do not attempt to pick or place an object whose presence or grasp state has not been verified.
[/PERSISTENT EXPERIENCE GUIDANCE]
